sentence: A 63-year-old woman with no significant history presented with a soft mass measuring 3 cm in diameter in the left parotid region with a history of 4 months, accompanied by peripheral paralysis of the cervical branch of the facial nerve with deviation of the commissure. ipsilateral labial The tumor, mobile and painless, was easily evident with bimanual palpation and was predominantly intraoral.
The patient did not have significant palpable lymphadenopathy in the neck and the rest of the physical examination was unremarkable.
In consultation with Neurology, the possibility of central facial paralysis was ruled out through a brain computed tomography scan.
The soft tissue ultrasound revealed a solid heterogeneous mass with soft tissue density in the parotid region and without the presence of lymph nodes of the adenomegallic range in the neck.
The fine needle aspiration puncture under ultrasound control was reported as negative with blood material on 2 occasions.

It was then decided to perform a frozen biopsy under general anesthesia with an intraoral approach through which the tumor was accessible by protruding under the oral mucosa next to the ostium of the Stenon's duct.

After incising the mucosa, a loose tumor was found, wine-red in color, with a vascular appearance, which was removed without difficulty through the same incision, verifying its continuity with the normal parotid tissue.
The frozen biopsy reported a lesion compatible with a benign vascular tumor.
The mucosa was closed with separate polyglycolic acid sutures and the procedure was completed.
The evolution was favorable with hospital discharge after 24 hours and complete recovery of facial paralysis 10 days after surgery.
She has no evidence of disease after 5 years of follow-up.
The deferred histological report was parotid capillary hemangioma.
